title: Phone Number Format Validation with SIMILAR TO
description: Find all contacts whose phone number does **not** match the standard format `XXX-XXX-XXXX` (three digits, dash, three digits, dash, four digits). These are data quality issues that need fixing.
solution_sql: SELECT contact_id, name, phone FROM contacts WHERE phone NOT SIMILAR TO '[0-9]{3}-[0-9]{3}-[0-9]{4}' ORDER BY contact_id

test_cases.description: Invalid formats: Bob(555.123.4567), Dave((555) 345-6789), Frank(5556789012), Hank(+1-555-678-9012), Jack(ext.5) — 5 invalid contacts

hints: Use SIMILAR TO with the pattern '[0-9]{3}-[0-9]{3}-[0-9]{4}' to match exactly three digits, a dash, three digits, a dash, and four digits.
Use NOT SIMILAR TO to find rows that FAIL the pattern — these are the invalid phone numbers needing correction.
explanation: SIMILAR TO (PostgreSQL) uses SQL regex where [0-9]{3} means exactly 3 digits. Valid format: 555-123-4567 ✓, 555-234-5678 ✓, 555-456-7890 ✓, 555-567-8901 ✓, 555-789-0123 ✓, 555-890-1234 ✓ (wait, Jack has 'ext.5'). Actually Alice(1), Carol(3), Eve(5), Grace(7), Ivy(9) are valid. Bob(dots), Dave(parens+space), Frank(no dashes), Hank(+1 prefix), Jack(ext suffix) are invalid → 5 invalid contacts.
